description.value: This study used modulated voxel-based morphometry of high-resolution T1-weighted structural MRI data to examine gray-matter relationships to diagnostic group and trait impulsivity in gambling disorder, cocaine-use disorder and healthy comparison participants.

spans.text: This study combines categorical (diagnosis-based) and dimensional (transdiagnostic) approaches to identify neural structural alterations linked to addiction subtypes and trait impulsivity, respectively, across individuals with gambling disorder (n=35), individuals with cocaine-use disorder (n=37) and healthy comparison individuals (n=37).

description.value: Observational, cross-sectional comparison of gambling disorder, cocaine-use disorder and healthy comparison participants.

description.value: The SCID was used to establish DSM-IV diagnoses of pathological gambling and cocaine dependence and to determine psychosis and other exclusionary conditions.

spans.text: Primary inclusionary criteria included a DSM-IV diagnosis of pathological gambling for GD participants, and of cocaine dependence for CUD participants, based on structured clinical interview (SCID; ( First, Gibbon, Spitzer, Williams, 1995 ). Primary exclusionary criteria included head trauma or other contraindication to MRI scanning and a history of psychosis (as determined using the SCID).
Due to an equipment upgrade in 2009, data acquisition was performed using two 3T Seimens Trio scanners.
